sections.content: A good decision compares options, weighs advantages and disadvantages, considers consequences and identifies priorities. Use connectors to move from evidence to evaluation and finally to a decision.

items.spanish: La primera opción es más barata, pero la segunda es más segura.
items.english: The first option is cheaper, but the second is safer.

items.spanish: Por lo tanto, creo que la seguridad debe ser nuestra prioridad.
items.english: Therefore, I think safety should be our priority.

items.spanish: Si elegimos la segunda, tendremos que pagar más, pero reduciremos el riesgo.
items.english: If we choose the second, we will have to pay more, but we will reduce the risk.

items.spanish: Después de comparar las opciones, hemos llegado a un acuerdo.
items.english: After comparing the options, we have reached an agreement.

sections.content: Do not treat a decision as an isolated answer. Show the criteria and consequences that led to it.
